summary.name: Squash and Stretch (Motion Design and Cinematography). Explicit animation principle, not an independent art movement; the source directly describes this visual direction.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: plan anticipation, impact, compression or extension, rebound and settling. Deformation follows movement, preserves apparent volume and recognizable silhouette, and uses varied timing with short holds. Objects should not deform continuously.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: one hero object or logo needing a single expressive moment, or characters and kinetic type when deformation needs a drawing language. Inferred from source combinations: mascot explainers, onboarding loops, title cards and social intros with a few key actions.
summary.limitations: Explicit: basic XPBD does not provide fluid merging, plasticity, tearing, rigid-body contact or origami creases. Matter.js gives 2D rigid bodies, not soft-body deformation. The soft-body glass recipe is an approximation needing baked states. Uniform spring presets are rejected. Remotion is fallback only, with a recorded reason.
summary.palette: Background is scene_dependent; no exact palette was approved, and the status is reference_dependent_example. Illustrative tokens are background #F4EDDF, foreground #32444A, accent_1 #66978E and accent_2 #C78461, with gradients disabled. Foreground on background measures 8.745:1. Accents against foreground measure 3.096 and 3.348, so they are decorative only; body text belongs on the main background. Source reviews of two sampled-frame sources (1–8s) show saturated bodies on quieter fields. Those colors are examples, not tokens, and must be rechecked on composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit video key poses use a paused GSAP timeline: anticipation sy 0.85, stretch sy 1.25, impact sx 1.3 with sy 1/1.3 to preserve area, then rebound, a short hold and settle. The 3s preview has ball motion 0–1.6s, block hop 1.4–2.6s and a hold, with one object deforming at a time. Interactive pattern options (click/tap, pointer, scroll) are suggestions. Pointer exit does not undo a triggered transformation; reduced motion should jump to the settled pose. Video must not depend on live input.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified by this style, and audio_direction is advisory only. Options include restrained contact accents, ambience, music synchronized to impacts, or silence, chosen by topic and mood. No mandatory sound, genre, tempo or voice is set. Explicit user audio requirements take precedence. No audio asset is supplied, and no soundtrack has been created.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploaded assets are mandatory. The preview can use flat SVG shapes with explicit pivots at contact points. Gaze patterns need eye layers or a rig. Surface-growth patterns need prepared textures or sprites. Exact copy, fonts and images are unspecified; any text needs local font loading before rendering.
summary.combinations: Explicit: style-028 supports flat vector characters, using only the four primary tokens, with only the acting object deforming and pivots at contact. Explicit: style-093 supports kinetic typography, with word-group baseline pivots, one emphasis word per phrase and no continuous wobble. Use combinations only when the deformation needs them.
summary.productionApproach: Explicit split: SVG as style_renderer for shapes and masks; GSAP as motion_engine on one paused timeline; HyperFrames as the default render_pipeline for assembly, timing, validation and export. Remotion is a fallback only under its verified condition. Optional: chroma-js for color validation, Matter.js or XPBD for baked physics, and Three.js only for the soft-body recipe. Motion and visuals are owned by the style layers, not the pipeline.
